title: Cannot find op_type: "LayerNormalization" when converting an ONNX model with TensorRT 8.6
body: I am trying to convert unet.opt.onnx with trtexec using dynamic min, opt, and max shapes. I preload /workspace/out/libnvinfer_plugin.so, but conversion fails around a LayerNormalization operation and no engine is created. The command output identifies the executable as TensorRT v8503 even though I am trying to use TensorRT 8.6.

symptoms_visible: My trtexec conversion stops at a LayerNormalization operation and does not create the TensorRT engine.
The startup line in my original output says TensorRT v8503 even though I am trying to use TensorRT 8.6.
N0.label: N0 LayerNormalization conversion failure reported

symptoms_visible: This is the downloaded controlnet_opt.onnx model renamed to unet.opt.onnx.
The model converts when I do not use dynamic image shapes, but the dynamic-shape conversion fails at LayerNormalization.
N1.label: N1 model identity and dynamic-only failure established

symptoms_visible: A complete run from /workspace/out/trtexec identifies itself as TensorRT v8600, but the dynamic-shape model still fails while parsing LayerNormalization with a plugin-not-found assertion.
N2.label: N2 TensorRT 8.6 executable run confirmed

symptoms_visible: I can reproduce a similar LayerNormalization failure in the supplied Diffusion demo simply by adding --build-dynamic-shape.
My separately exported ControlNet model works without dynamic shapes and fails with dynamic shapes.
N3.label: N3 minimal dynamic-shape reproduction supplied

symptoms_visible: After recompiling TensorRT 8.6 and setting LD_LIBRARY_PATH to its shared libraries, the dynamic-shape conversion completes instead of stopping at the LayerNormalization plugin lookup.
N_terminal.label: terminal matching TensorRT libraries resolve conversion

question_patterns: The linked model is named controlnet_opt.onnx, while your command uses unet.opt.onnx. Can you confirm which model you are converting?
Did you rename the downloaded model, or is unet.opt.onnx a different export?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It is the right model. I renamed controlnet_opt.onnx to unet.opt.onnx.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: They are different models; unet.opt.onnx is another export that was not downloaded from that link.
It is the same model, but I kept the original controlnet_opt.onnx filename.

edges.comment: Issue comments c0-c3 on reporter dongjinxin123's system: the reporter confirms the downloaded ControlNet model was only renamed and then volunteers that static conversion succeeds while dynamic-shape conversion fails.

question_patterns: Your earlier startup line reports v8503. Can you run the intended executable and paste the complete startup line and failure output?
Which TensorRT version does the exact trtexec binary used for the failing run print?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran /workspace/out/trtexec and the complete log starts with 'TensorRT.trtexec [TensorRT v8600]'. The dynamic-shape conversion still reaches LayerNormalization and ends with 'Assertion failed: creator' and 'Plugin not found'.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The exact executable still prints TensorRT v8503; I do not have a v8600 trtexec binary in this environment.
The executable prints TensorRT v8601 rather than v8600, with the same plugin-not-found output.

edges.comment: Issue comments c6-c8 on the reporter's system: after the maintainer notices v8503 in the earlier output, the reporter supplies raw output from /workspace/out/trtexec showing v8600 and the same LayerNormalization plugin-creator failure.

question_patterns: Can you provide a smaller reproduction using one of the supplied TensorRT demos?
Is the failure reproducible without your standalone ControlNet export?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. In the supplied demo/Diffusion example, I run demo_txt2img.py for Stable Diffusion 1.5 and add only --build-dynamic-shape. That produces a similar LayerNormalization plugin-not-found error.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The supplied Diffusion demo works with --build-dynamic-shape; only my modified ControlNet export fails.
The demo reproduces with different prompt text but the same --build-dynamic-shape flag and error.

question_patterns: How did you export the standalone ControlNet ONNX model?
What changes did you make to the Diffusion demo to produce this model?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I changed demo/Diffusion, added the ControlNet model to model.py, and exported its ONNX model. The export converts correctly without dynamic shapes but gives the LayerNormalization error with dynamic shapes.

edges.comment: Issue comments c9-c11: the original reporter explains the export and supplies a simpler reproduction using the repository's Diffusion demo. Although another participant asks about exporting ControlNet, the setup and observed failures described here are the original reporter's own system.

solution.intent: Use a consistently built TensorRT 8.6 installation: recompile TensorRT 8.6, make its shared-library directory the active runtime library path, and rerun the dynamic-shape conversion to verify that the matching plugin and runtime libraries are loaded.
solution.concrete_example: Recompile the TensorRT 8.6 build, then set LD_LIBRARY_PATH to the directory containing that build's TensorRT .so files, for example `export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/path/to/TensorRT-8.6/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. Run the same dynamic-shape command again and confirm that it creates the engine without the LayerNormalization plugin-not-found assertion.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter states the operational resolution—recompile TensorRT 8.6 and set LD_LIBRARY_PATH to its .so files. Interpreting the mixed v8503/v8600 evidence and missing plugin creator as a mismatch between the selected executable and runtime-loaded TensorRT libraries is engineer-side inference.

edges.comment: Issue comments c13-c14 from reporter dongjinxin123 provide the accepted self-resolution: TensorRT 8.6 must be recompiled and LD_LIBRARY_PATH set to its shared libraries. Later comments describe separate users, versions, models, and opset workarounds and are intentionally excluded from the opening reporter's causal chain.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause as an inconsistent TensorRT runtime environment: invoking a TensorRT 8.6 executable or preloading one plugin library was insufficient while the matching TensorRT 8.6 shared libraries were not selected through LD_LIBRARY_PATH.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: the original v8503 startup line, the later v8600 executable log with the same missing plugin-creator assertion, and reproduction of the dynamic-only failure in the supplied Diffusion demo.
Must recommend recompiling or otherwise using a consistent TensorRT 8.6 build and setting LD_LIBRARY_PATH to that build's .so directory before rerunning the conversion.
Must not present changing ONNX opset, running ONNX simplification, disabling dynamic shapes permanently, or writing a custom LayerNormalization plugin as the accepted fix for this reporter's case.
Must have the reporter verify that the same dynamic-shape conversion creates the engine with the matching libraries before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable machine-learning developer who can modify TensorRT Diffusion demo code, export ONNX models, build TensorRT from source, configure dynamic optimization profiles, and inspect verbose trtexec logs.
persona_hint.communication_style: Persistent and hands-on; shares long commands and raw logs, answers version and model-identity questions directly, develops a simpler reproduction, and ultimately reports the environment fix independently.
